June 19, 1939. Morning Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese-owned Chinese language newspaper):

"BRITISH SOLDIERS AT THE GREAT WESTERN ROAD SUB-STATION
OF THE SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT POLICE BUREAU COMPLETELY
WITHDRAWN : BARBED WIRE BARRICADES VOLUNTARILY REMOVED"

The Great Western Road Sub-Station of the
Western District Branch of the Shanghai City Government was
unlawfully closed by the British military authorities on
January 5. As its existence is necessary for the
maintenance of peace and order in that area, the Branch
Police Bureau the other day detailed policemen to re-open
the main gate of the sub-station. This met with unlawful
interference from the British defence force and a tense
situation ensued.

FILE
Subsequently, an agreement was reached between
Mr. "Niu-Keh", the Officer-in-Charge of Bubbling Well
Police Station, and Wong Tuh-ling (王德林), the Chief of
the Branch Police Bureau.

It is learned that at 1.20 p.m. June 18, the
British soldiers were completely withdrawn, while the
barbed wire barricades were voluntarily removed.

On June 18, Sergeant Ma Wen-sin (馬文辛) and
nine police constables from the Zikawei Branch Police
Bureau were detailed to the sub-station.

1939年6月19日。晨间译文。

《新顺报》（日资中文报纸）：

“上海市政府警察局大西路分所的英军士兵全部撤离：铁丝网路障自愿拆除”

上海市政府西区分局大西路分所于1月5日被英国军事当局非法关闭。鉴于该分所的存在对于维持该地区治安秩序实属必要，分局警察局日前派遣警员重新开启分所大门。此举遭到英国防卫部队的非法干涉，导致局势紧张。

存档
随后，静安寺捕房主管“牛克”先生与分局警察局局长王德林达成协议。

据悉，6月18日下午1时20分，英军士兵全部撤离，同时铁丝网路障被自愿拆除。

6月18日，徐家汇分局警察局的马文辛警长及九名巡警被派往该分所。

Memorandum on Shanghai City Government Police Bureau
Sub-Station Great Western and Columbia Roads

On June 17, 1939, information was received by
the Municipal Police to the effect that members of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau had gained
entry into the sub-station situated at the junction
of Great Western and Columbia Roads, by breaking down
the rear door. This act was in contravention of a
decision of the British Defence Sector Commander and
the British military were informed, following which a
guard was left outside the premises.

At 1.57 p.m. the same day a further message
was received stating that a large party of Shanghai
City Government Police Bureau personnel armed with
rifles and "mausers" had arrived at the sub-station,
and that several police constables were engaged
demolishing the barbed wire barricades erected by
the British Military at the front entrance of the
station, whilst the remainder were deployed along
the foot-path on either side of the roadway.
Immediately following receipt of this message, the
Commissioner of Police, and senior officials of the
Municipal Police were informed; the Reserve Unit
was called out.

Following the arrival of Police and British
Military details, the officer in charge of the
Shanghai City Government Police Bureau personnel was
advised to withdraw his unit into the sub-station;
Superintendent Wong of the same body was later
interviewed, when he was informed of the British
military requirements by the Deputy Commissioner
(Divisions). After subsequent negotiations with

1939年6月17日，工部局警务处收到情报称，上海市政府警察局人员砸开后门，进入了位于大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处的分所。此举违反了英国防区司令的决定，遂通知英军，随后在建筑物外留下了守卫。

同日下午1时57分，又收到消息指出，一大群携带步枪和“毛瑟枪”的上海市政府警察局人员抵达该分所，几名巡警正在拆除英军在分所正门设置的铁丝网路障，其余人员则部署在道路两侧的人行道上。收到此消息后，立即通知了警务处处长及工部局警务处高级官员；后备队被召集出动。

Major Ashmore, Brigade Major, it was decided to allow
the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau to function
provided (1) that no police use the roadway outside
the station; (2) that police patrols use the rear
door and side entrance during the course of their
duties. These conditions were referred to Lieut.-
Colonel Igarashi, who after consultation with
Superintendent Wong, agreed with the provisions.
The latter officer revisited the sub-station later

旅参谋长阿什莫尔少校商定，决定允许上海市政府警察局运作，条件是 (1) 任何警察不得使用分所外的道路；(2) 巡逻警察在执行任务期间使用后门和侧门。这些条件提交给五十岚中校，他在与王督察协商后，同意了这些规定。该警官于当天晚些时候再次视察分所，并据此指示工作人员。

在上海市政府警察局当局接受上述条款后，英军拆除了分所的路障。

1939年6月17日，工部局警务处收到情报，称上海市政府警察局人员砸开后门，进入了位于大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处的巡捕房。此举违反了英军防区司令的决定，遂通知英军，随后在建筑物外留下了卫兵。

同日下午..57分（原文如此），又收到进一步消息，称一大群携带步枪和“毛瑟枪”的上海市政府警察局人员抵达该巡捕房，数名警员正在拆除英军在巡捕房正门设置的铁丝网路障，其余人员则部署在道路两侧的人行道上。收到此消息后，立即通知了警务处处长及工部局警务处高级官员；后备队被召集出动。

随着警务人员和英军分队抵达，被告知上海市政府警察局带队军官将其队伍撤入巡捕房内；随后会见了该局的黄（Wong）督察长，由副警务处长（分区）向其告知英军的要求。经与

Shanghai Municipal Police,
June 18, 1939.

SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT SUB-STATION, GREAT WESTERN ROAD.

The status of the City Government Police Sub-Station at
the Junction of Great Western and Columbia Roads yesterday
became the subject of negotiations between the S.M.P. and the City
Government Police. These negotiations have now been concluded to
the satisfaction of both parties.

The British troops in whose defence sector the sub-station
lies have been withdrawn from the immediate vicinity of the sub-
station following the successful conclusion of the negotiations
between the respective police authorities.

The City Police are to be permitted to occupy the building
with police constables. They have undertaken not to function
outside the front of the building adjoining the Municipal road
and that for their movements they will utilize the side entrance
having access into City Government Territory . In consideration
of this undertaking the barbed wiring has been removed from the
front entrance of the building.

上海公共租界工部局警务处，
1939年6月18日。

上海市政府大西路巡捕房。

昨日，位于大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处的市政府警察巡捕房的地位问题，成为工部局警务处与市政府警察之间谈判的主题。目前谈判已结束，双方均感满意。

在该巡捕房所属防区内驻守的英军，在各方警察当局成功结束谈判后，已撤离巡捕房附近区域。

市政府警察获准派警员进驻该建筑物。他们承诺不在毗邻公共租界道路的建筑物正面之外执行公务，并且在行动时将利用通往市政府辖区的侧门。鉴于此项承诺，建筑物正门的铁丝网已被拆除。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JUN 19 1939

Settlement
Is Reached
On Station

City Government Police
Will Not Function On
Municipal Roadway

After lengthy negotiations on
Saturday and yesterday morning
between the Shanghai Municipal
Police, on behalf of the British
Military authorities, and the City
Government Police, a settlement
was reached on the status of the
Shanghai City Government Sub-
Station at the junction of Great
Western and Columbia Roads.
In a communique issued yester-
day, the Shanghai Municipal Police
announced that the negotiations
have now been concluded to the
satisfaction of both parties. The
settlement was reached after the
City Government Police undertook
not to function outside the front
of the building adjoining the Muni-
cipal road and that for their move-
ments they will utilize the side en-
trance having access into City
Government Territory.
On Saturday a tense situation
developed on the scene as from
about midnight on Friday night
Chinese policemen of the City
Government moved into the police
station, which had been closed by
the British military authorities at
the beginning of the year. At
about two o'clock in the afternoon,
about 100 fully armed City Gov-
ernment policemen assembled there.
Reinforcements of East Surreys and
Shanghai Municipal Police were
called out and rushed to the scene
in trucks. Upon request of the
British military, the City Govern-
ment policemen withdrew to their
territory. Later the British au-
thorities decided to place barbed
wiring in front of the building, but
did not do so when it was learnt
that negotiations were progressing
smoothly. Guards of East Surreys
and Shanghai Municipal Police
were maintained outside the Sub-
Station throughout Saturday night
and yesterday morning until a
settlement was reached.
In the official announcement, the
Shanghai Municipal Police states:
"The British troops, in whose de-
fence sector the sub-station lies,
have been withdrawn from the im-
mediate vicinity of the sub-station
following the successful conclusion
of the negotiations between the re-
spective police authorities.
"The City Police are to be per-
mitted to occupy the building with
police constables. They have un-
dertaken not to function outside
the front of the building adjoining
the Municipal road and that for
their movements they will utilize
the side entrance having access
into City Government Territory
In consideration of this undertak-
ing the barbed wiring has been
removed from the front entrance
of the building."

《字林西报》
1939年6月19日

就巡捕房
达成协议

市政府警察
将不在公共租界
道路上执勤

经过周六及昨日上午上海公共租界工部局警务处（代表英军当局）与市政府警察之间的长时间谈判，就位于大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处的上海市政府巡捕房的地位问题达成了协议。
工部局警务处在昨日发布的公报中宣布，谈判现已结束，双方均感满意。在市政府警察承诺不在毗邻公共租界道路的建筑物正面之外执行公务，并且在行动时将利用通往市政府辖区的侧门之后，达成了这一协议。
周六，现场局势紧张，自周五午夜左右起，市政府的中国警察进入了年初被英军当局关闭的警察局。下午两点左右，约100名全副武装的市政府警察在那里集结。东萨里团（East Surreys）和工部局警务处的增援部队被召集，并乘卡车赶赴现场。应英军要求，市政府警察撤回其辖区。后来，英方当局决定在建筑物前设置铁丝网，但在得知谈判进展顺利后并未实施。整个周六夜间及昨日上午，直到达成协议为止，东萨里团和工部局警务处的卫兵一直在巡捕房外维持警戒。
在官方公告中，工部局警务处声明：“在该巡捕房所属防区内驻守的英军，在各方警察当局成功结束谈判后，已撤离巡捕房附近区域。”
“市政府警察获准派警员进驻该建筑物。他们承诺不在毗邻公共租界道路的建筑物正面之外执行公务，并且在行动时将利用通往市政府辖区的侧门。鉴于此项承诺，建筑物正门的铁丝网已被拆除。”

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JUN 18 1939

〔右上角印章及手写内容：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE ... No. S. B. D. ... Date ____ 〕

Police Sub-station Again
Occupied By Chinese

Junction Of Great Western And Columbia Roads
Scene Of Parleys Yesterday; Police Leave
On Request; Amicable Settlement Seen

A certain amount of tension prevailed in the western outside area yesterday, following the re-occupation by the City Government Police of the Sub-Station at the junction of Great Western and Columbia Roads at about midnight on Friday night by way of the back entrance. The station was closed early this year by the British Military.

Tension reached its peak shortly after 2 o'clock yesterday afternoon when, in addition to about 40 fully armed City Government policemen, who were in the Sub-Station and vicinity, another 60 men crossed Great Western Road, from the Fah Hwa Village East, and joined them. The few sentries of the East Surrey Regiment and the Settlement Police, who were on guard outside the station at the time, were reinforced, and, upon the request of the British Military the City Government Policemen withdrew.

Negotiations were being carried on from early morning until late last night by Inspector F. W. Dudley, officer in-charge of Bubbling Well Police, and Colonel Wang, officer-in-charge of City Government Police in that area with a view to coming to an understanding. The negotiations were being conducted by the Shanghai Municipal Police on behalf of the British Military. No settlement was reported as Colonel Wang had to report to his superiors, but it is understood that that the City Government police have been asked not to use the front door on Great Western Road but the back door in their own territory.

At about 3.45 yesterday afternoon, British Military trucks drove up with barbed wire and iron rods. The British soldiers immediately commenced to nail up the sub-station door and windows and drove rods into the ground in preparation to barricade the station.

Shortly after 4 o'clock the order was cancelled, in view, it is understood of the favourable progress of negotiations. The British Tommies removed the barbed wire and iron rods. Most of the British troops and Settlement Police were withdrawn by 4.40 p.m., several remaining on guard outside the police station to see that no City Government policemen operated along the Settlement road, which is in the British Defence Sector.

Ranking officers of the Shanghai Municipal Police headed by Deputy Commissioner H. M. Smith, O.B.E., and Assistant Commissioner A. H. Samson were on the scene, in addition to Major B. H. Ashmore, British Brigade Major, and Major S. R. Hunt, Liaison Officer with the Japanese Forces.

It is understood that the British Military maintain that the City Government police cannot function along a Settlement Road in the British Defence Sector and have requested the City Government to keep the door of the Sub-Station leading on to Great Western Road closed.

British officials last night were confident that an amicable settlement would be agreed upon.

中国警察再次
占领警察巡捕房

大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处
昨日成为谈判场所；警察应请求撤离；有望达成友好和解

昨日，在市政府警察于周五午夜左右通过后门重新占领位于大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处的巡捕房后，西部越界筑路地区出现了一定程度的紧张局势。该巡捕房于今年早些时候被英军关闭。

昨日下午2点过后不久，紧张局势达到顶峰，当时除了已在巡捕房及附近的约40名全副武装的市政府警察外，另有60人从法华村东（Fah Hwa Village East）穿越大西路加入他们。当时在巡捕房外站岗的几名东萨里团和租界警察哨兵得到增援，应英军要求，市政府警察撤离。

静安寺巡捕房主管 F. W. Dudley 督察与该地区市政府警察主管王（Wang）上校从清晨至深夜一直进行谈判，以期达成共识。谈判由工部局警务处代表英军进行。据报道，由于王上校需向上级汇报，尚未达成和解，但据悉，市政府警察已被要求不使用大西路的前门，而是使用其辖区内的后门。

昨日下午约3点45分，英军卡车运载着铁丝网和铁杆驶抵。英军士兵立即开始钉封巡捕房的门窗，并将铁杆打入地下，准备封锁巡捕房。

下午4点后不久，据悉鉴于谈判进展顺利，命令被取消。英国士兵（Tommies）移走了铁丝网和铁杆。大部分英军和租界警察于下午4点40分撤离，仍有数人留在警察局外站岗，以确保没有市政府警察在属于英军防区的租界道路上行动。

工部局警务处的高级官员在现场，由副警务处长 H. M. Smith 爵士（O.B.E.）和助理警务处长 A. H. Samson 率领，此外还有英军旅参谋长 B. H. Ashmore 少校和日军联络官 S. R. Hunt 少校。

据悉，英军坚持认为市政府警察不能在英军防区内的租界道路上执行公务，并要求市政府保持通往大西路的巡捕房大门关闭。

英国官员昨晚确信将达成友好和解。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JUN 1 8 1939

Minor Incident at
“Ta Tao” Station
British Troops on Duty
On Great Western Road ;
Negotiations Under Way

Men of the East Surrey Regiment were on duty on the South side of Great Western Road near Columbia Road up to a late hour last night, opposite the “Ta Tao” police station which members of that force opened at 6.10 a.m. yesterday, after it had been barricaded off in January by order of the British Military authorities. Negotiations between the British Command and the Japanese authorities were understood to have been under way since late yesterday afternoon with a view to coming to some agreement, and indications were that an amicable settlement of the fate of this station would be reached probably some time today.

As will be recalled, the station was barricaded off in such a manner as to close any exit unto Settlement roads and the “Ta Tao” authorities were given to understand at the time that the front door could be used by uniformed men, as this was contrary to previous agreements made between the authorities concerned.

Ta Tao Police Enter, Leave

Yesterday’s incident started when at 6.10 a.m., a number of Ta Tao policemen opened the barricaded front-door and established themselves in the station. The British military authorities in whose sector that part of the Settlement is situated, were informed and a steel-helmeted party of soldiers was posted near the building, the Ta Tao policemen being asked to leave, which they did.

No untoward incident occurred until 1.50 p.m. when two truck-loads carrying 60 members of the same force, armed with rifles and pistols, arrived and walked across to their station, after British sentries had been withdrawn. Troops were again rushed to the scene and following a conversation between a British officer and the Chinese officer in charge of the policemen, the latter withdrew, marching along Great Western Road in an easterly direction.

At 3 p.m. Major-General F. K. Simmons, Commanding Officer of British Forces in Shanghai, arrived at the scene and remained a few minutes, talking with officers standing near the police station whilst two Japanese military photographers were busily engaged in taking pictures from a distance, particularly of the sentries in front of the station and the four truck-loads of British soldiers along Columbia Road.

The Reserve Unit of the Shanghai Municipal Police had also been ordered to stand by at Bubbling Well Police station, but was not sent to the scene as their services were not required. Amongst police officers who were there at various times during the afternoon, were Major K. M. Bourne, Commissioner. Capt. H. M. Smythe, Deputy-Commissioner in charge of Divisions and, Assistant Commissioner A. H. Samson who is temporarily in charge of “B” Division.

《字林西报》，

1939年6月18日

“大陶”巡捕房发生小事件
英军在大西路执勤；
谈判正在进行中

昨晚直至深夜，东萨里团（East Surrey Regiment）的士兵一直在哥伦比亚路附近的大西路南侧执勤，对面是“大陶”巡捕房。该巡捕房由该部队成员于昨日清晨6点10分开启，此前曾于今年一月奉英国军事当局命令被封锁。据悉，自昨日下午晚些时候起，英军指挥部与日本当局之间一直在进行谈判，以期达成某种协议，且有迹象表明，关于该巡捕房命运的友好解决方案可能将于今日某个时间达成。

如前所述，该巡捕房被以封锁通往租界道路的所有出口的方式加以 barricaded（设障封闭），当时“大陶”当局获悉，身着制服的人员可以使用正门，因为此举违背了有关当局之间先前达成的协议。

大陶警察进入后离开

昨日的事件始于清晨6点10分，当时数名大陶警察打开了被封锁的正门并进驻巡捕房。位于该租界区域的英国军事当局得知情况后，派遣一队头戴钢盔的士兵在建筑物附近布防，并要求大陶警察离开，他们随即照办。

此后未发生任何意外事件，直到下午1点50分，两辆卡车运载着60名同属该部队的成员抵达，他们携带步枪和手枪，在英国哨兵撤走后，步行前往他们的巡捕房。军队再次紧急赶赴现场，经过一名英国军官与负责指挥警察的中国军官交谈后，后者率队撤离，沿大西路向东行进。

下午3点，驻沪英军司令F. K. Simmons少将抵达现场，停留数分钟，与站在巡捕房附近的军官交谈，而两名日本军事摄影师则忙于从远处拍摄照片，特别是拍摄巡捕房前的哨兵以及沿哥伦比亚路排列的四卡车英军士兵。

上海公共租界工部局警务处的后备队也奉命在静安寺巡捕房待命，但因无需其服务而未派往现场。下午不同时段在场的警官包括：警务处长K. M. Bourne少校、负责各分区事务的副警务处长H. M. Smythe上尉，以及暂时负责“B”分区的助理警务处长A. H. Samson。

Wiring Countermanded

At 3.45 p.m. barbed wire was un-
loaded from military trucks and a
group of twenty soldiers donned
leather gloves to erect another bar-
ricade. They had hardly begun their
work, however, when they were
ordered to stop and the barbed wire
was removed.

At various intervals during the
afternoon, Japanese officers in plain
clothes and uniforms, passed the
scene in motor-cars but none of them
alighted.

At 9 p.m. yesterday evening, three
British sentries were stationed on
the other side of Great Western Road,
whilst one foreign and three Chinese
members of the S.M.P. were on duty
in front of the building and a tent
had been pitched in a British-owned
garden on the south side of Great
Western Road, where British soldiers
detailed for duty at that point made
themselves at home.

The immediate vicinity of the
station was devoid of pedestrian
traffic although this had not been
closed and a barbed wire barricade
had been placed at the entrance of
the alleyway adjoining the station,
although it was so placed that per-
sons living in the lane had free
access.

架设铁丝网命令被撤销

下午3点45分，军用卡车上卸下铁丝网，一组二十名士兵戴上皮手套准备架设另一道屏障。然而，他们刚开始工作，便接到停止命令，铁丝网随后被移除。

下午的不同时段，身着便服和制服的日本军官乘车经过现场，但无人下车。

昨晚9点，三名英国哨兵被部署在大西路另一侧，而一名外籍和三名为上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）服务的华籍警员在建筑物前执勤，并在大西路南侧的一个英属花园内搭起帐篷，被指派在该点执勤的英国士兵在此安顿下来。

巡捕房附近区域没有行人通行，尽管该区域并未封闭，且在毗邻巡捕房的弄堂入口处设置了铁丝网屏障，但其设置方式使得居住在弄堂内的人员仍可自由出入。

CHINA PRESS
MAR 1 5 1939

Ta Tao Police
Patrol Evicted
On Brenan Rd.

British Military Unit
And S.M.P. Squad
Make Request

An armed patrol composed of
members of the Ta Tao police was
evicted from Brenan Road, near
Edinburgh Road, early last night,
by the British Military authorities
and the Shanghai Municipal Police,
squads of both bodies making their
appearance on the scene simul-
taneously.

It was learned from authoritative
sources that the Ta Tao policemen
left immediately after they had been
requested to do so by a British senior
military officer, and that they main-
tained a friendly attitude through-
out the negotiations.

The incident occurred at about 8:15
p.m., when a number of Ta Tao
policemen were observed patrolling

1939年3月15日

大陶巡逻队
在布伦南路被驱逐

英军部队
与工部局警务处小队
提出要求

昨晚早些时候，由大陶警察组成的武装巡逻队在爱丁堡路附近的布伦南路（Brenan Road）被英国军事当局和上海公共租界工部局警务处驱逐，双方的小队同时出现在现场。

据权威消息来源获悉，大陶警察在英国高级军官要求他们离开后立即撤离，并且在整个谈判过程中保持了友好的态度。

事件发生在晚上8点15分左右，当时有人观察到大陶警察正在布伦南路巡逻。一辆载有英军部队的卡车和一辆封闭式警车突然沿路驶来，停在一些大陶警察附近。当一名陆军军官与伪政权官员交谈时，英国士兵（Tommies）和工部局警务处的外籍警员在道路两侧列队。

经过简短交谈后，大陶警察离开布伦南路，通过附近的一条弄堂进入日军占领区。

额外意义

英国军事当局昨日的行动具有额外的意义，这源于美国海军陆战队指挥官J. C. Fegan上校最近提出的反对，即反对便衣日本宪兵侵入美军防区，以及周日海军陆战队队员和上海公共租界工部局警务处人员驱逐了一伙此类人员。

尽管上海公共租界工部局昨日宣布，Fegan上校并未就日本宪兵违反工部局警务处与日本海、陆及外交当局之间达成的谅解而 irregularly（违规）进入租界区域一事提出正式抗议，但有报道称，海军陆战队总部对所谓工部局接受日本行动的做法感到强烈不满。

工部局昨日发布了另一份关于与日本当局达成协议的公报，强调上海公共租界工部局警务处在租界内的完整性。

然而，尽管有此公告，经查明，日本便衣宪兵已在租界内进行多次突袭，且至少有十二名中国人在未经租界警察许可的情况下被“绑架”。

Shanghai Special Municipality

The Shanghai Municipal Council has again assumed a "challenging attitude in interfering with the functions of the Greater Shanghai Special Municipality" the "Tairiku Shimpo" charged yesterday.

According to the daily, Mr. R. W. Yorke, Assistant Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police has informed the chief of the western district section of the Greater Shanghai Special Municipality that he had been ordered hereafter to prohibit entrance and passage of police constables of the Reformed Government into alley-ways on both sides of extra-settlement roads.

Questioned on receipt of a report of the order, Mr. Fu Siao-en, Mayor of the Shanghai Special Municipality, sought confirmation of the report from Mr. C. S. Franklin, Chairman of the Shanghai Municip-

al Council, who said he had not heard of it, but would inquire into it, the daily said.

Adding further fuel to the controversy, the journal asserted, it was rumoured that at meeting a few days ago, the Municipal Council had adopted a resolution stating it would not recognize collection of salt taxes by the Reformed Government on extra-settlement roads. This action would lead to non-recognition of not only salt taxes but of every other tax, the daily contended.

At a time when the closure of a western district police sub-station has not been settled, this attitude of the Municipal Council is raising trouble without cause, the daily said, adding that it is now receiving serious consideration from the Reformed Government.

数周前，公共租界当局和英国防卫军非法关闭了上海特别市政府位于大西路的警察分驻所。此举意在故意阻碍“维新政府”和上海特别市政府的影响力。然而，此后工部局与“维新政府”之间又发生了新的争端。1月25日，静安寺警察局主管警官通过日本特务机关上海西区支部向上海特别市政府发送了一份便函，告知一项官方通知，即不允许上海特别市政府雇用的任何警察穿越租界道路。收到此通知后，傅筱庵市长与工部局主席富兰克林先生进行了谈判，后者表示他对此事不知情，并在调查后将给予答复。据收到的消息，工部局已决定不承认“维新政府”征收盐税。因此，预计今后工部局将阻碍“维新政府”的所有税收征管工作。目前，上海特别市政府和“维新政府”在其日本顾问的协助下，正考虑采取积极步骤来应对工部局的非法压迫。

Following the closing by the British Defence
Force of a sub-police station of the Shanghai Special
Municipal Government at the corner of Great Western Road
and Columbia Road in the extra-Settlement road area in
the Western District of Shanghai, Loo Ying ( 盧 英 ),

to Mayor Fu Hsiao-en who subsequently lodged protests with
the British Consulate-General and the S.M.C.
Of late, it has been widely reported in
Japanese circles that the sub-police station had already
resumed functioning and that the Shanghai Special
Municipal Government was collecting taxes in the western
area.
Our reporter made an investigation in the
district and found the said sub-police station still
closed, while the puppet policemen who had been staying
in a small house next to the station had disappeared.
Thus the Japanese reports are all untrue.

TAKES DEFINITE STEPS TOWARDS BRITAIN'S CHALLENGE-LIKE
ACT : JAPANESE RESIDENTS FRETTING AT THE OVER PRUDENCE
OF THE AUTHORITIES".

The incident caused by the unlawful closing
of a Chinese sub-police station on Great Western Road
on the orders of the Commander of the British Defence
Force must be interpreted not only as wilful disregard
of the Shanghai Special Municipal Government by the
British authorities but also as a challenge to Japan
which is supporting the Government. Five days have
elapsed since the incident took place, yet the Shanghai
Special Municipal Government has not taken any steps
through over-prudence. The delay in taking proper steps
is causing a section of educated Chinese and Japanese
residents to hold the view that effective and suitable

lesson to Britain for she is growing too presumptuous. It

after a careful investigation has been made. A pre-war-

delay in dealing with the unlawful action of the British
soldiers would mean tacit consent. For this reason, both
Chinese and Japanese residents are holding strong views
about the matter. It is reported that a number of
important Japanese and Chinese residents are considering
the holding of a mass meeting to encourage the authorities.

High officials of the "Reformed Government,"
Japanese residents and Chinese supporters of the "Reformed
Government" have become highly indignant over the closing
of a Chinese sub-police station on Great Western Road.
On January 9, the "China Press", an English language
paper, bluntly published an article containing a denial
of our report on the violent action committed by the
British soldiers.

Major Ashmore, Commander of a section of the British
Defence Force, on that day stated as follows regarding
the incident:-

(1) The closing of the police station was not
effected by the British soldiers but by the police officers
of the station.

(2) That no photograph of Premier Konoye was
seen on the wall when the British soldiers left (?) entered)
the station.

(3) That there certainly was a five-barred flag,
but a British soldier carefully took it down and handed it
to a Chinese police officer.

(4) That no police officer was assaulted.

Thus Major Ashmore has denied everything.
However, a reporter of this paper has seen with his own
eyes a five-barred flag which had been hacked to pieces

the police officers of the station? A police officer informed

The Great Western Road Outpost (No.1173 Great
Western Road) of the Western District Branch of the
Police Bureau of the "Shanghai City Government"
(92 Jessfield Road) was closed by the British Military
on January 5, 1939. This outpost was first established
sometime in 1930 by the former Shanghai City Government
and staffed with one officer and some ten constables.
The staff of the branch police offices within the British
Perimeter were disarmed by the British Military during
August 1937, when the Japanese Forces continued their
drive on Chapei, but the disarmed members were allowed
to stay on the premises until November 1, 1937 when they
evacuated. When the so-called "Shanghai Dao Dao City
Government" (now known as "Shanghai City Government")
was inaugurated in December, 1937, the outpost in
question was again occupied by the Police Bureau of the
said government and has since been functioning until
its recent closure by the British Military.

JAN 13 1939

No Protest Made Yet
On British Closure
Of “Ta Tao” Station

Up to a late hour last night no protest has been received by the local British authorities from the “Provisional Government” with regard to the closing of a puppet police station on Great Western Road by the British military.

It is believed, however, that if such a protest will be made by the Nanking puppet regime, it will be ignored.

It is further reported that a note, the nature of which was not disclosed yesterday, was received by the British Consul-General from “Mayor” Fu Hsiao-an, head of the “Municipality of Greater Shanghai.”

A party of East Surreys closed and barred a “Ta Tao” police post on Great Western Road, near Columbia Road, on the morning of January 5. The post was closed, it was stated, because it was on a Settlement Road and consequently well within the British defense sector.

CHINA PRESS
JUL 10 1939

Hongkew Paper
Claims British
Army “Bandits”

Military Authorities
Stand By Statement
In CHINA PRESS

Charges made by the Hongkew Japanese daily Tairiku Shimpo that British soldiers in closing the “Ta Tao” police station at Great Western Road last Thursday had committed “banditry” were ignored yesterday by the British Military authorities.

British army chiefs, it was learned last night, had nothing to add to the statement published yesterday morning in THE CHINA PRESS on the matter, and they could see no reason to discuss it further.

In an interview with THE CHINA PRESS, Brigade-Major B. H. Ashmore previously denied that alleged vandalism had been committed by troops in his charge during the closure of the station.

It was denied that a five-barred flag was torn up, and that a clod of mud had been flung at a picture of Prince Konoye, said by Japanese newspapers to have been hanging on the wall of the station.

Carried Out Quietly

It was also stated that the closure of the station had been carried out quietly, and during the performance of their duties, the British soldiers had maintained most amicable relations with officers of the “Ta Tao” government.

The station was closed, it was pointed out during the course of the interview, because it faced an outside road within the British Military sector.

Japanese Attack

The Tairiku Shimpo yesterday bewailed the attitude taken by the British military authorities concerning the closing of the Great Western Road sub-police station of “Greater Shanghai Municipality” last Thursday.

Branding it as “banditry,” the newspaper stated that the British military authorities, by contending that Britain did not recognize the “Greater Shanghai Municipality,” were trying to justify their action “by insulting the five-barred flag of the ‘Reformed Government’ atop the police sub-station.”

“How can they possibly explain their generosity in allowing the same flag to be hoisted atop the Customs building on the Bund?”, the daily queried. “They maintain the illegality of the location of the police station on an extension road. Then why don’t they close up the Japanese gendarmerie sub-station on extension roads in Western Shanghai?” asks the Japanese editorial.

Survey Given

Giving an historical survey of the acquisition of the extension roads, the Japanese daily pointed out that legally, the Shanghai Municipal Council was not empowered to exercise administrative rights, including policing and taxation, in alleyways and lanes abutting upon extension roads and over the houses on and facing these streets, not to speak of the roads proper.

“The British authorities committed vandalism under the pretence that they executed a right delegated to them. They resorted to violence without any notice whatever to the Municipal Council authorities, and we are at a loss to find better terms than to describe their action as a grave insult which cannot be ignored in the light of law as well as morality,” declared the daily.

“The incident concerns directly the ‘Greater Shanghai Municipality,’ which it is hoped, will take appropriate measures against the British authorities. We would like to notify the British authorities that we Japanese, as the closest friend of the ‘Reformed Government,’ have a strong determination, and are fully prepared to deal with wrong-doers. It all depends on the future attitude of the British authorities,” concluded the Tairiku Shimpo.

称英军为“匪徒”

军方坚持
《字林西报》中的声明

虹口日文日报《大陆新报》指控英军上周四在关闭大西路“大道”警察局时犯下“匪行”，英国军方当局昨日对此不予理会。

据悉，昨晚英国陆军高层表示，对于昨天早晨《字林西报》就此事项发表的声明，他们无话可补充，也看不出有任何理由进一步讨论。

旅参谋长B. H. 阿什莫尔此前在接受《字林西报》采访时否认，其麾下部队在关闭该局期间实施了所谓的故意破坏行为。

报道否认了五色旗被撕毁的说法，也否认了有人向日本报纸所称悬挂在局内墙上的近卫公爵照片投掷泥块的说法。

平静执行

采访中还指出，该局的关闭是平静执行的，英军士兵在执行任务期间，与“大道”政府的官员保持了最友好的关系。

采访中指出，该局被关闭是因为它面向英国军事防区内的一条外部道路。

日本的攻击

《大陆新报》昨日对英国军方当局就上周四关闭“大上海特别市”大西路分警察局所采取的态度表示哀叹。

该报将此标榜为“匪行”，并称英国军方当局声称英国不承认“大上海特别市”，试图通过“侮辱警察局分所顶上的‘维新政府’五色旗”来为其行为辩护。

“他们如何解释允许同一面旗帜悬挂在外滩海关大楼顶部的慷慨之举？”该日报质问。“他们坚持认为警察局位于越界筑路上的位置是非法的。那么，他们为何不关闭位于上海西部越界筑路上的日本宪兵分所呢？”该日文社论问道。

提供概况

该日文日报在回顾越界筑路的获取历史时指出，从法律上讲，上海工部局无权在毗邻越界筑路的弄堂和巷子里，以及在这些街道之上和面向这些街道的房屋上行使包括警务和征税在内的行政权利，更不用说道路本身了。

“英国当局以行使授予他们的权利为借口，实施了故意破坏行为。他们在未通知工部局当局的情况下诉诸暴力，我们找不到比这更好的措辞来形容他们的行为是对法律和道德都无法忽视的严重侮辱，”该日报宣称。

“此事直接关系到‘大上海特别市’，希望其能针对英国当局采取适当措施。我们要通知英国当局，我们日本人作为‘维新政府’最亲密的朋友，有着坚定的决心，并已充分准备对付不法之徒。这完全取决于英国当局未来的态度，”《大陆新报》总结道。

January 10, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

News Digest and other local newspapers :-

MAJOR ASHMORE'S STATEMENT ON THE CLOSING OF POLICE
STATION ON GREAT WESTERN ROAD.

In connection with the action of the
British military authorities in closing the Western
District Police Station of the Police Bureau on Great
Western Road near Columbia Road on the morning of January 5,
the Japanese newspapers in Shanghai have been publishing
articles attacking the action of the British military
authorities and declaring that the destruction of the
photograph of Prince Konoye, the former Premier of the
Japanese Government, constituted an insult to Japan.
On January 8, Major Ashmore issued the
following statement on the closing of the police station
in question :-
"On the morning of January 5, acting on
orders, I proceeded to the Western District to close the
police station of the Police Bureau. I led a party
to execute the order. It was the policemen themselves
who removed their uniforms etc. I was present at the
time but I did not see any photograph of Prince Konoye
nor of any other printed photos or documents.
As to the five-barred flag, the British
soldiers handed it to a policeman. At the time of
closing the house, the British soldiers did nothing
insulting to the policemen or embarrassing to them.
Deputies of the Japanese newspaper organizations took
photographs of the place and made an investigation; they
may know the truth. What is being said in the Japanese
newspapers is entirely untrue. It is reported that the
bogus government will lodge a protest with me and this
may probably materialize.
"I did meet a Japanese gentleman who asked
me to give a reason for closing the police station.
I told him that as the site of the police station of
the Police Bureau is located in the Settlement and
furthermore as the place lies within the defence sector
of the British defence force, we had the right to close
it and its closing was not improper. I told the
Japanese gentleman that the British soldiers have
always observed neutrality in their defence sector
since the outbreak of local hostilities in 1937 and
no army of any nationality were allowed to pass through
this sector. On the withdrawal of the Chinese forces
from Shanghai, the Chinese soldiers that sought shelter
in the Settlement were allowed to pass through the
British defence sector only after they had been disarmed.
This is impartial. It would be too far fetched to say
that the closing of the police station was directed
against the Japanese."

阿什莫尔少校关于关闭大西路警察局的声明。

鉴于英国军方于1月5日上午关闭了位于哥伦比亚路附近大西路的警务处西区警察局，上海各日文报纸纷纷发表文章，抨击英国军方的行动，并宣称损毁日本政府前首相近卫文麿公爵的照片构成了对日本的侮辱。1月8日，阿什莫尔少校就关闭该警察局一事发表了如下声明：

“1月5日上午，我奉命前往西区关闭警务处的警察局。我率领一队人员执行命令。是警察们自己脱下了制服等物品。当时我在场，但我没有看到任何近卫公爵的照片，也没有看到其他任何印刷照片或文件。

至于五色旗，英国士兵将其交给了一名警察。在关闭房屋时，英国士兵没有做出任何侮辱警察或令其难堪的行为。日本报社的代表对该地点进行了拍照和调查；他们可能了解真相。日本报纸上的说法完全不实。据报道，伪政府将向我提出抗议，这很可能会成为事实。

“我确实会见了一位日本绅士，他要求我说明关闭警察局的理由。我告诉他，由于警务处警察局的所在地处于租界内，而且该地位于英国防卫部队的防区内，我们有权关闭它，其关闭并非不当。我告诉这位日本绅士，自1937年当地敌对行动爆发以来，英国士兵在其防区内始终保持中立，任何国籍的军队均不得通过该区域。在中国军队撤离上海时，寻求进入租界避难的中国士兵只有在解除武装后才被允许通过英国防区。这是公正的。如果说关闭警察局是针对日本人，那就太牵强附会了。”

January 8, 1939.
TAIRIKU SHIMPO

"CLOSING OF CHINESE POLICE STATION ON GREAT
WESTERN ROAD BY BRITISH SOLDIERS"

A representative of the Shanghai
Special Municipal Government requested an interview with
Major-General Telfer-Smollett, Commander of the British
Defence Force, on January 5, but the request was rejected.
On January 6, the representative was received by Major
Ashmore.

In the course of the interview,
Major Ashmore stated to the representative that the police
station in question was closed because it was located
on a Municipal road, which is not a Chinese administrative
area for it is located in the British sector. Furthermore,
the Shanghai Special Municipal Government's Police Bureau
is not recognized by Britain.

The representative stated to the
British officer that the police station in question had
existed at that place prior to the hostilities and that
the station had been taken over by the new city government
for more than a year. He asked on what ground the
British authorities, without giving any notice beforehand, had
closed the station. He held the British authorities
responsible for the humiliation caused to his national
flag.

The British officer replied that
it was the right of the British authorities to close the
station at any time when found necessary and that there
was no necessity to give notice beforehand. The
officer stated that as regards the flag affair an
investigation would be made.

Alas! Policemen assaulted, Premier Konoye's

JANUARY 7, 1939.

MAINICHI

"BRITISH AUTHORITIES VIOLENTLY CLOSE DOWN TA TAO POLICE
STATION ON GREAT WESTERN ROAD"

Great Britain has been actively engaged during the
past few years in creating a rupture between Japan and China.
She caused much indignation among Japanese people and Govern-
ment by rendering assistance to the Chiang Kai Shek regime
following the outbreak of hostilities.

On January 5 the British authorities closed down
a Ta Tao Police Station on Great Western Road by means of
force and in the name of the British army.

The Branch Police Station on Great Western Road
was in existence prior to the outbreak of hostilities and the
house number plate was affixed by the former City Government.
Thus the existence of the branch police station on Great
Western Road was an established fact recognized by the various
authorities as well as by the S.M.C.

At 10 a.m. January 5 several armed British soldiers
suddenly appeared at the police station in question and on
the orders of General Smollet they closed down the station
on the ground that the station is located on the boundary line.

After unlawfully removing the police officers and
the furniture from the station, and lowering the five barred
flag, the soldiers left the place.

Highly indignant over the action of the British
soldiers, the police officers of the station reported the
incident to Police Headquarters. The action of the British
soldiers is regarded as a challenge to the "Reformed
Government" and the Japanese authorities.

P.A.&B.C.(Sh.B.)

1939年1月7日。

《每日新闻》

“英国当局武力关闭大西路大道警察分局”

过去几年，英国一直积极从事破坏日中关系的活动。战事爆发后，她通过援助蒋介石政权，引起了日本民众和政府的极大愤慨。

1月5日，英国当局以英军名义，使用武力关闭了大西路的一处大道警察分局。

大西路分警察分局在战事爆发前就已存在，门牌号码由前市政府悬挂。因此，大西路分警察分局的存在是一个既定事实，得到了各方当局以及工部局（S.M.C.）的认可。

1月5日上午10点，几名武装英军士兵突然出现在该警察分局，并根据斯莫利特（Smollet，音译）将军的命令，以该分局位于边界线上为由将其关闭。

在非法移除分局内的警察和家具，并降下五色旗后，士兵们离开了该地。

分局警察对英军士兵的行动感到极为愤慨，将此事件报告给警察总局。英军士兵的行动被视为对“维新政府”和日本当局的挑战。

P.A.&B.C.(Sh.B.)

“工部局年度报告暴露其自私行径”

《每日新闻》以上述标题发表以下社论：——

昨日，工部局发布了关于1938年行政工作的年度报告。在阅读了报告中涉及日本人的事项后，我们感到工部局过于自我吹嘘，从而给人一种不愉快的感觉。

报告中有几件事项值得商榷。关于虹口问题，工部局直接或间接地表达对日本的恶感。我们认为工部局以这种方式表达是在行事自私。战事爆发时，工部局放弃了其在虹口地区的所有行政工作，并在日军占领上海后，通过日本当局的好意接管了该地区部分行政工作。工部局似乎在此事上无谓地对日本怀有恶感，应当反思其行为。多愁善感固然无妨，但他们必须考虑如果虹口立即开放，局势将会如何。目前，苏州河南岸正发生各种反日活动，尽管法租界的局势更为严重。1938年间，苏州河南岸发生了20多起反日恐怖行为，而工部局为此采取的应对措施令日本当局不满意。

CHINA PRESS.
JAN 9 1939

Police Station
Closing Rouses
Nippon Papers

Alleged Vandalism Is
Refuted By British
Authorities

Denying allegations in the local Japanese press that mud was thrown on a picture of Prince Ayamaro Konoye, former Premier of Japan, last Thursday when British troops closed the police sub-station of the "Greater Shanghai Municipality," Brigade Major B. H. Ashmore yesterday emphasized that there were no pictures in the sub-station at the time it was closed.

"I was in personal charge during the entire time that the dismantling of the station was being carried out," he said, "And the actual work was done by the 'Ta Tao' policemen themselves. They showed no resentment.

"No picture of Prince Konoye or anyone else was in evidence."

Flag Carried Away

Replying to the Japanese press assertion that a five-barred flag of the "Reformed Government" was torn to pieces, he stated, "The flag was noticed just as everyone was about to depart and as an act of courtesy a British soldier took it down and handed it to the 'Ta Tao' policemen intact."

To the charge that a Chinese Constable of the "City Government" service was beaten by several British soldiers, Major Ashmore declared "The dismantling of the station was carried on in perfect orderliness and no one was molested.

The Japanese journals are further reported by a semi-official Japanese news agency to have devoted much space and to have severely criticized the British authorities for what they termed the "arrogant" attitude of Brigade Major Ashmore when he received the representative of the "Greater Shanghai Municipality."

Japanese Called

"I received a Japanese gentleman when he called at the British Military Headquarters to ask our reasons for closing the police sub-station," Major Ashmore said, "and I told him that the station was in the British defense sector and abuts on a Municipal Road. I explained that the sub-station was closed chiefly for these reasons.

"The display of a five-barred flag in the British Defense Sector, I further told him, might be a source of provocation and was considered undesirable by the British Military Authorities.

"Then I pointed out to the Japanese gentleman that at the outbreak of the hostilities in 1937, the British troops had disarmed the Chinese troops in this district for the purpose of protecting the lives and property of foreigners and Japanese alike.

"In consequence of this previous action, I then carefully elucidated to my caller, that the British Military Authorities do not recognize the 'Tao Tao' police in this area.

"The discussions were carried on in an atmosphere of courtesy and friendliness."

"This act of vandalism should be answered by decisive steps on the part of Japan," the Shanghai Mainichi is reported by a Japanese news agency to have declared in its editorial yesterday.

"It can be said that the British authorities resorted to action of the most malignant kind," the Nippon journal is reported to have continued.

"The British Authorities," Major Ashmore stated, "in closing this police sub-station in no way directed their action against the Japanese. On the contrary they consider it the logical procedure in view of their former action in disarming the police constables and soldiers of the National Government."

Referring to traditional British politeness, the Shanghai Mainichi concludes stating, "Unlike the actions of a trivial nature which have taken place in the past, this incident can be viewed in the same light as the 'assist Chiang Kai-shek and resist Japan' policy which Great Britain has been pursuing.

"At any rate this episode of British violence is one that should not be passed over lightly by Japan."

FILE

1939年1月9日

警察分局
关闭引发
日本报纸关注

英国当局
驳斥所谓破坏行为

针对当地日本报刊声称上周四英军关闭“大上海市政府”警察分所时向日本前首相近卫文麿亲王的照片投掷泥巴的指控，旅少校 B. H. Ashmore 昨日强调，分所关闭时内部并无任何照片。

“在整个拆除分所的过程中，我亲自负责指挥，”他说，“实际工作是由‘大道’警察自己完成的。他们没有表现出任何怨恨。

“现场并没有近卫亲王或其他任何人的照片。”

旗帜被带走

针对日本报刊声称“维新政府”的五色旗被撕碎的断言，他陈述道：“就在大家准备离开时注意到了这面旗帜，出于礼貌，一名英国士兵将其取下，并完好无损地交给了‘大道’警察。”

对于指控称几名英国士兵殴打了一名“市政府”服务的华籍巡捕，Ashmore 少校声明：“分所的拆除工作秩序井然，无人受到骚扰。

据一家半官方的日本通讯社报道，日本期刊进一步花费大量篇幅，严厉批评英国当局，称旅少校 Ashmore 在接见“大上海市政府”代表时态度“傲慢”。

召见日本人

“当一位日本绅士来到英国军事总部询问我们关闭警察分所的理由时，我接待了他，”Ashmore 少校说，“我告诉他，该分所位于英国防区，且毗邻一条公共租界道路。我解释说，分所关闭主要是出于这些原因。

“我还告诉他，在英国防区内展示五色旗可能会成为挑衅的来源，英国军事当局认为这是不可取的。

“随后，我向这位日本绅士指出，在1937年战事爆发时，英军曾解除该地区中国军队的武装，目的是保护外国人和日本人的生命财产。

“鉴于此前的这一行动，”他接着向来访者仔细阐明，“英国军事当局不承认该地区的‘大道’警察。

“讨论是在礼貌和友好的气氛中进行的。”

“日本应采取果断措施回应这种破坏行为，”据一家日本通讯社报道，《上海每日新闻》昨日的社论如此宣称。

“可以说，英国当局采取了最恶毒的行动，”据报道，该日本报刊继续说道。

Ashmore 少校表示：“英国当局在关闭该警察分所时，其行动绝非针对日本。相反，鉴于他们此前解除国民政府警察巡捕和士兵武装的行动，他们认为这是合乎逻辑的程序。”

提及传统的英国式礼貌，《上海每日新闻》总结道：“与过去发生的琐碎性质的行动不同，此次事件应被视为与英国一直推行的‘助蒋抗日’政策同等看待。

“无论如何，日本不应轻易放过这次英国暴力事件。”

Soldiers Refuted

“Ta Tao” Station Closed
Without Incident

Japanese press that the small party
of British soldiers which closed a
“Ta Tao” police station in Great
Western Road last Thursday, tore a
“Reformed Government” flag to

士兵的指控

“大道”分所关闭
未生事端

英国军事当局昨日明确否认了当地日本报刊散布的指控，这些指控称上周四在大西路关闭“大道”警察分所的一小队英国士兵撕碎了“维新政府”的旗帜，向日本前首相近卫亲王的照片投掷泥巴，并殴打了隶属于该分所的一名华籍巡捕。

对关闭警察局一事表示愤慨
据称日中当局正考虑针对英国此举采取行动

据《上海每日新闻》昨日报道，日本和中国当局对英军于周四上午关闭位于大西路与哥伦比亚路交界处的上海特别市警察分署的举动感到愤怒，并将该行动解读为“对其职权的直接挑战”。

这家日本日报称英国的行动是“非法”的，并指出该警察分署是由前上海特别市政府在目前的敌对状态发生之前设立的，且已得到租界及其他外国当局的承认。该报宣称，该警察局悬挂的是上海特别市的门牌号码，而非工部局（S.M.C.）的号码。

《每日新闻》称，相关的日本和中国当局仍在进行调查，以便就此事件采取“坚决态度”。

据该日报报道，由于这一行动是在英军司令 A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett 少将的命令下执行的，日中官员在周五晚间讨论此事时声称，此事不能不了了之。

CHINA PRESS.

JAN 7 1939

Protests Not
Expected On
Station Case

British Military Await
No Repercussions
From Puppets

No protest from the "Ta Tao
Government" or its Japanese spon-
sors has been lodged over the
closure by the British military of a
puppet police station on Great
Western Road at the Columbia Road
intersection. Nor is any protest
expected.
British military authorities con-
tend that the station was located
within the British defense sector,
being off a Settlement road. There-
fore, it is held, the British military
were well within their rights to
close the station without consulting
anyone in advance.
The station was closed by order
of Major-General A.P.D. Telfer-
Smollett Thursday morning by
Major B. H. Ashmore, Brigade
Major of the British Forces here,
and a party of soldiers of the East
Surrey Regiment.
The station, a single-story build-
ing, was at the time occupied by
several puppet policemen, all in
civilian clothes. These offered no
resistance and left quietly when
ordered to do so.
For nearly 90 minutes the Tom-
mies were engaged in scaling up
the premises. They removed the
furniture, bedding, uniforms, cloth-
ing, batons and everything else in
the building and piled all articles
up neatly outside on the pavement.
The doors and windows were closed
and locked, while those windows
facing the country were sealed with
barbed wire.
Notices in Chinese and English
were posted. These notices, an-
nouncing that "This house has been
closed by order of the British
Military Forces," were still there
yesterday.
Miscellaneous furniture was still
on the street yesterday.

英军当局声称，该警局位于英军防区内，且偏离租界道路。因此，他们认为，英军有权在未事先与任何人协商的情况下关闭该警局。
周四上午，根据A.P.D. 特尔弗-斯莫利特（A.P.D. Telfer-Smollett）少将的命令，驻沪英军旅长副官B. H. 阿什莫尔（B. H. Ashmore）少校率领一队东萨里团（East Surrey Regiment）士兵关闭了该警局。
该警局为一座单层建筑，当时由几名身着便服的伪警察占据。这些人未作抵抗，在接到命令后安静地离开。
英军士兵花了近90分钟时间对该处所进行封锁处理。他们搬走了家具、寝具、制服、衣物、警棍以及楼内所有其他物品，并将所有物品整齐地堆放在外面的人行道上。门窗被关闭并上锁，面向乡野一侧的窗户则用铁丝网封死。
现场张贴了中英文告示。这些告示宣布“本房屋已奉英军命令关闭”，截至昨日仍张贴在原处。
昨日，各种家具仍堆放在街道上。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS.

JAN 6 1939

“Ta Tao” Station
Shut by British

Soldiers Leave Little in
Great Western Road Post;
Uniforms Put on Road

Because it was actually on a Settlement road within the British Military Defence sector, a station of the so-called “Ta Tao” police in Great Western Road at Columbia Road, was closed by the British military yesterday morning.

“Closed” in this case meant a thorough job. A party of British soldiers of the East Surrey Regiment, accompanied by Maj. E. H. Ashmore, Brigade Major, arrived at the scene at 10 o’clock to carry out Maj.-Gen. A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett’s orders. They found the one-storey building occupied by a group of “Ta Tao” policemen, all in plain-clothes. These offered no resistance, and left quietly.

The entire eviction and sealing-up took about an hour and a half. All the furniture, bedding, uniforms, clothing, batons and what-not of the “Ta Taoists” were carried out of the rooms and placed in neat piles outside the walls. The main, barred door was carefully closed and locked. Other doors and windows, including those facing the countryside behind the station, were closed and barbed wire was draped over them in thorough fashion.

Notices Posted

Then notices, in English and Chinese, were posted prominently on the entrances. The announcement in English read: “This house has been closed by order of the British Military Forces.”

All this having been accomplished, and the “Ta Tao” defenders of the law having wandered off, the party of British soldiers departed, leaving behind only the ghost of a police station.

1939年1月6日

“大道”警察局
被英军关闭

大西路警岗所剩无几；
制服弃置路旁

由于该所谓“大道”警察位于哥伦比亚路的大西路警局实际上处于英军防区内的租界道路上，昨日上午被英军关闭。

此处的“关闭”意味着彻底清理。东萨里团的一队英士兵在旅参谋长 E. H. Ashmore 少校的陪同下，于十点钟抵达现场，执行 A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett 少将的命令。他们发现这栋单层建筑内有一群便衣“大道”警察占据。这些人未作抵抗，安静离去。

整个驱逐和封存过程耗时约一个半小时。“大道”人员的所有家具、寝具、制服、衣物、警棍及其他杂物均被搬出房间，在墙外整齐堆放。装有铁栏的正门被仔细关闭并上锁。其他门窗，包括面向警局后方乡野的那些，均已关闭，并严密地覆盖上铁丝网。

随后，入口处醒目地张贴了中英文告示。英文公告写道：“本房屋已奉英军命令予以封闭。”

至此一切处置完毕，“大道”执法者们四散离去，英军小队也随之撤离，只留下一座警局空壳。
